item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Concentra, a major occupational medicine provider, will open its first Pensacola location this month, expanding workplace health services across the region. The ribbon-cutting is set for Wednesday, Oct. 14 at 10 a.m. at 6235 North Davis Highway, Suite 113, with local business and community leaders expected to attend. The new medical center will…
item.content:encoded:
Concentra, a major occupational medicine provider, will open its first Pensacola location this month, expanding workplace health services across the region. The ribbon-cutting is set for Wednesday, Oct. 14 at 10 a.m. at 6235 North Davis Highway, Suite 113, with local business and community leaders expected to attend.

The new medical center will offer occupational health services tailored to employers in aviation, aerospace, advanced manufacturing, defense, healthcare, financial services, maritime, and other industries. Services include work injury care, physical therapy, Department of Transportation physicals, pre-placement exams, medical surveillance, respirator fit testing, and drug and alcohol screening.

This marks Concentra's 41st medical center in Florida. The company says the Pensacola location addresses growing demand for specialized workforce health services among area employers and their employees.

item.title: Archaeologists discover three 1559 shipwrecks off Pensacola coast
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The wrecks are tied to the ill-fated voyage of Tristán de Luna y Arellano, according to reporting from Yahoo News. De Luna's fleet originally consisted of 11 ships…
item.content:encoded:
Researchers have identified three shipwrecks off the coast of Pensacola dating back to 1559, offering new insights into one of the earliest European expeditions to reach Florida.

The wrecks are tied to the ill-fated voyage of Tristán de Luna y Arellano, according to reporting from Yahoo News. De Luna's fleet originally consisted of 11 ships carrying approximately 1,500 people, making it one of the largest colonization attempts in the region during the Spanish colonial period.

The discovery adds to the historical record of early European exploration along the Gulf Coast and underscores Pensacola's role in that era. The wrecks could provide valuable archaeological evidence about 16th-century maritime technology, supplies, and the fate of de Luna's expedition, which ultimately failed to establish a permanent settlement.

item.content:encoded:
Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Vote-by-mail ballots are beginning to reach Northwest Florida voters ahead of the November general election.


The latest state figures show nearly 25-thousand ballots have already gone out in Escambia County, with Republicans and Democrats requesting them in nearly equal numbers. Another 67 Escambia ballots had already been returned as of the latest report.

Santa Rosa County's mailing was still ramping up when the figures were compiled.


The deadline to register for the November third election is next Monday, October fifth.

item.title: Santa Rosa Chief Deputy Randy Tifft discusses suicide prevention, emerging opioid, Flock cameras and jail operations
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Santa Rosa County, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Santa Rosa County Chief Deputy Randy Tifft joined Pensacola’s Morning News Monday, discussing issues ranging from mental health and drug overdoses to the removal of Flock license-plate cameras and a recent murder-for-hire case. Suicide prevention and first responders With September recognized as Suicide…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Santa Rosa County Chief Deputy Randy Tifft joined Pensacola’s Morning News Monday, discussing issues ranging from mental health and drug overdoses to the removal of Flock license-plate cameras and a recent murder-for-hire case.


Suicide prevention and first responders

With September recognized as Suicide Prevention Awareness Month, Tifft said Santa Rosa deputies encounter suicide and attempted-suicide calls frequently, sometimes on a daily basis.


He said those incidents also take a toll on deputies, detectives and crime-scene personnel who repeatedly respond to traumatic scenes.

The Sheriff’s Office uses grant funding for a mental health counselor, and Tifft said every employee meets with the counselor once a year, with additional sessions available at no cost.


Emerging opioid appearing locally

Tifft said the Sheriff's Office has encountered cychlorphine, an emerging synthetic opioid, in Santa Rosa County.


“We have seen some of it in our area, not as much as it has across the country in certain places,” Tifft said.


He described the drug as “very dangerous and very deadly” and expressed concern about substances being mixed with other drugs.


Flock cameras being removed

Santa Rosa deputies no longer have access to the Flock automated license-plate reader system, according to Tifft.


He said Sheriff Bob Johnson ordered the system shut off following direction from Gov. Ron DeSantis. Flock contractors are now removing the physical cameras, although Tifft said some may remain standing while that statewide process continues.


“Ours are not in use,” Tifft said. “None of our deputies can access Flock.”


Corrections officers and jail staffing

Tifft also discussed the often-overlooked role of corrections officers, calling them the “unsung heroes” of law enforcement.


He said Santa Rosa County pays corrections officers at the jail the same as patrol deputies, a policy intended to help the agency recruit and retain qualified officers.


Perdue murder-for-hire case

The interview also touched on the Stephanie Perdue case. Tifft said investigators gathered additional evidence after Perdue was jailed, when she continued efforts to have her husband killed.


He credited investigators and the State Attorney’s Office for developing the case and securing a conviction.


Tifft closed by noting Santa Rosa deputies will join State Rep. Michelle Salzman for a food distribution Wednesday at Welcome Church in Pace.    Pasted text

item.title: Taddeo Campaign Launches Spanish-Language WhatsApp Channel for Florida Voters
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Democratic nominee for Florida Chief Financial Officer Annette Taddeo has launched a new Spanish-language WhatsApp channel called Taddeo2Day, aimed at connecting directly with Hispanic voters across the state ahead of November's election. The channel will provide subscribers with notifications about upcoming campaign events, updates, and election…
item.content:encoded:
Democratic nominee for Florida Chief Financial Officer Annette Taddeo has launched a new Spanish-language WhatsApp channel called Taddeo2Day, aimed at connecting directly with Hispanic voters across the state ahead of November's election.

The channel will provide subscribers with notifications about upcoming campaign events, updates, and election information in Spanish. Taddeo said the move reflects where many Hispanic families already communicate. "WhatsApp is how so many Hispanic families communicate every day, and we're using it to connect with voters in Spanish, share important election information, and make sure our community knows when and where to vote," she said in a statement.

The launch comes as Hispanic voters have emerged as a key focus in this year's midterm elections. According to a September 22 analysis by The New York Times, Democrats lead Republicans by 35 percentage points among Hispanic likely voters in national polling — 64 to 29 percent — underscoring the growing importance of engaging Hispanic communities before November.

Taddeo, who was born and raised in Colombia before immigrating to the United States, made history in 2017 as the first Latina Democrat elected to the Florida Senate. She is the only Latina on the Democratic ticket this cycle and is running on three campaign priorities: affordability, accountability, and anti-corruption.

A portion of Robinson Point Road in Santa Rosa County is closed today for cross drain replacement, Santa Rosa County officials announced.

The closure extends from just north of 3375 Robinson Point Road to south of 3388 Robinson Point Road. Work began at 7:30 a.m. Monday and is expected to wrap up by close of business Tuesday, September 29, weather permitting.

Drivers heading through the area can detour via Garcon Point Road in both directions. Santa Rosa County has posted a detailed map of the closure online at santarosa.fl.gov.

item.title: Santa Rosa County Fall Events: Pumpkin Patches, Concerts, Markets Light Up Season
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County is rolling out a full slate of fall activities through November, with something for every age and interest. Families looking for classic autumn fun can head to Holland Farms Pumpkin Patch & Maze near Milton, open daily through November 1, which offers hayrides, an 8-acre corn maze, zip lines, train rides, and a free cup of boiled…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County is rolling out a full slate of fall activities through November, with something for every age and interest.

Families looking for classic autumn fun can head to Holland Farms Pumpkin Patch & Maze near Milton, open daily through November 1, which offers hayrides, an 8-acre corn maze, zip lines, train rides, and a free cup of boiled peanuts with admission. Sweet Season Farms, also near Milton, runs its 18th annual corn maze and pumpkin patch on weekends through November 8, featuring over 25 farm activities, u-pick sunflowers in October, and food vendors including a farm bakery.

For live music, Bands on the Blackwater offers free outdoor Friday-night concerts downtown Milton from 7 to 9 p.m. through October, with performances by Symphonic Thunder, Bone Dry Band, Anthony Crawford, Blackwater Country, and The Modern Eldorados. Meanwhile, Adventures Unlimited in the Blackwater River State Forest near Milton offers canopy zip-line tours and canoeing through November, plus cabin and campsite stays for those wanting an overnight adventure.

Shoppers will find the Highway 87 Outdoor Market in Navarre running the first and third Saturday of each month from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m., featuring farm-to-table vendors and crafts. Sand Dollar Plaza in Navarre hosts "Party in the Plaza" Saturdays from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m. with merchant specials and community events. For details on any event, Santa Rosa County Communications & Media Relations provides contact information and websites for each venue.

item.dc:creator: newsroom

The Gulf Breeze, Jay, Milton, Navarre, and Pace library branches will maintain six-day-a-week service under the revised schedule. Mondays and Saturdays will run from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m.,…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County's five public libraries will shift to new operating hours beginning Monday, October 5th, according to a announcement from county communications.

The Gulf Breeze, Jay, Milton, Navarre, and Pace library branches will maintain six-day-a-week service under the revised schedule. Mondays and Saturdays will run from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m., while Tuesday through Friday hours extend from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. All branches will be closed on Sundays.

The Family History and Research Center and the Library Administration office will keep their existing hours unchanged. For specific branch locations and additional details, residents can visit www.santarosa.fl.gov/libraries or call (850) 981-7323.

item.content:encoded:
Gas prices across Florida jumped 18 cents over the past week, but the Pensacola area continues to enjoy some of the state's cheapest fuel.

According to reporting from the Orlando Sentinel, Pensacola drivers are paying $4.08 per gallon on average — well below the state's most expensive markets. West Palm Beach and Boca Raton top the list at $4.52 per gallon, followed by Naples at $4.48 and Gainesville at $4.43.

Northwest Florida fares better overall. Panama City is averaging $4.11 per gallon, while Crestview-Fort Walton Beach sits at $4.12 — making the entire region among the state's most affordable places to fill up.

item.title: UWF professor lands $543K NIH grant to study dopamine's role in immune response
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A University of West Florida researcher has secured federal funding to investigate how dopamine affects the body's inflammatory response, with potential applications for treating diseases like rheumatoid arthritis and Alzheimer's. Dr. Peter Cavnar, associate dean and associate professor at UWF's Hal Marcus College of Science and Engineering,…
item.content:encoded:
A University of West Florida researcher has secured federal funding to investigate how dopamine affects the body's inflammatory response, with potential applications for treating diseases like rheumatoid arthritis and Alzheimer's.

Dr. Peter Cavnar, associate dean and associate professor at UWF's Hal Marcus College of Science and Engineering, received a $543,756 grant from the National Institute of General Medical Sciences over four years. The award will support research exploring how dopamine and dopamine receptors regulate neutrophils — the most common type of white blood cell in the immune system — and their role in controlling inflammation.

Neutrophils serve as the immune system's first line of defense against infection, but when overactivated, they can damage tissue and contribute to autoimmune and neurodegenerative diseases. Cavnar's team hopes that understanding dopamine's influence on neutrophil behavior could lead to new treatments for conditions including rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, and Alzheimer's disease. Dopamine-targeting drugs already treat a range of conditions from Parkinson's disease to schizophrenia, but their effects on the immune system remain poorly understood.

The grant, formally titled a Support for Undergraduate Research Excellence (SuRE) award, is designed to build research capacity by involving undergraduate students as active participants rather than observers. Cavnar emphasized that UWF's research strength lies in student-driven investigation, with undergraduates receiving direct financial support to work as genuine collaborators on original scientific questions.

No injuries were reported in connection with the incident.

The closure ran from midnight to 5 a.m. CDT, with helicopter operations remaining unaffected during that window. The alert, issued by the FAA Airport Updates account on Bluesky, did not specify a…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola Regional Airport (PNS) was closed to fixed-wing aircraft operations early Monday morning, according to an FAA alert posted to social media. The closure ran from midnight to 5 a.m. CDT, with helicopter operations remaining unaffected during that window.

The alert, issued by the FAA Airport Updates account on Bluesky, did not specify a reason for the closure. It's unclear whether the restriction was weather-related, operational, or tied to runway maintenance or other airport work.

PNS typically handles regional commercial and general aviation traffic. The brief, early-morning window minimized disruption to scheduled flights, most of which operate during daylight hours.

item.content:encoded:
Pensacola area weather this week begins with pleasant, crisp conditions before moisture returns, according to the National Weather Service.

Monday will be sunny with a high near 87 and calm northeast winds around 5 mph. Overnight, expect clear skies and a low around 59 with calm winds — a comfortable setup for anyone planning outdoor activities.

The pattern shifts later in the week as rain chances increase, though details on timing and intensity aren't yet specified. If you're heading outside early in the week, it'll be an ideal window before the moisture moves in.

item.content:encoded:
An Escambia County Sheriff's Office search in the Cottage Hill area on September 17 has led to two arrests, according to court documents revealing investigators suspect foul play in an active missing person investigation.

Details about the missing person's identity, the specific charges against those arrested, or the nature of the suspected foul play were not immediately available. The ECSO search appeared to be connected to the disappearance, though a full accounting of the investigation's timeline and findings has not yet been disclosed.

The case remains active. Anyone with information about the missing person or the circumstances surrounding the disappearance is urged to contact the Escambia County Sheriff's Office.

Statewide, gas prices have been volatile in recent days. Florida saw prices jump 18 cents last week before declining 6 cents over the weekend, according to AAA data cited in the…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County continues to offer the cheapest fuel in Florida, with an average price of $4.08 per gallon as of Sunday, according to reporting from North Escambia.

Statewide, gas prices have been volatile in recent days. Florida saw prices jump 18 cents last week before declining 6 cents over the weekend, according to AAA data cited in the report.

The Pensacola metro area's lower pump prices compared to the rest of the state offer some relief to local drivers as fuel costs remain a significant household expense across the region.

item.content:encoded:
Atmore police are investigating an incident that began with a physical altercation and escalated into gunfire in the city's restaurant corridor.

According to WKRG News 5, the incident unfolded at the Waffle House parking lot, where someone was reportedly pistol whipped during a fight. The situation then moved to a nearby Popeye's Louisiana Kitchen location, where the suspect allegedly discharged a firearm.

Atmore Police Department has not yet released details about injuries, arrests, or the circumstances leading to the confrontation. The investigation is ongoing.

item.content:encoded:
A pleasant autumn pattern is settling over the North Escambia area this weekend, with sunny skies and a high near 88 expected Sunday, according to the National Weather Service. Winds will remain calm, picking up only slightly to around 5 mph from the northwest in the afternoon.

Sunday night will stay mostly clear with temperatures dropping to near 60, providing relief from the summer heat. The cooler, drier air mass moving into the region is expected to stick around through the start of the week, bringing below-normal overnight temperatures and low humidity levels that should make outdoor activities comfortable.
